rounds.text: German Green Steel & Power Ltd trades at an attractive P/E of 10.4x [E1] and 10.13x against a sector benchmark of 21.26x [E5], alongside a low EV/EBITDA of 6.32x compared to the sector benchmark of 12.25x [E10]. The company demonstrates fundamental strength with a 3-year compounded profit growth of 26% [E15], trailing twelve months profit growth of 27% [E16], and a robust multi-year return on equity track record, featuring a median 3-year ROE of 24% [E18] and a current ROE of 21.4% [E12]. Operating margins have also expanded meaningfully to 10% in Mar 2026 from 5% three years prior [E20], supported by strong cash generation where operating cash flow reached Rs 141 Cr in Mar 2026 with a cash conversion ratio of 1.76x [E24, E25]. Furthermore, a discounted cash flow model indicates substantial intrinsic value with a large margin of safety, and a reverse DCF implies the market is pricing in a negative -0.9% earnings growth against a base case assumption of 18.0% [E35, E36, E37]. Conceded: the current ratio sits at 0.97x indicating short-term liability pressures, borrowings have ticked up to Rs 375 Cr in Sep 2026, and the dividend yield is 0.00% [E3, E28, E29].

Despite seemingly attractive headline metrics, German Green Steel & Power Ltd carries notable financial and operational risks that warrant caution. Most concerningly, the company exhibits a current ratio of 0.97x as of March 2026, indicating that current liabilities exceed current assets [E28]. This short-term liquidity pressure is compounded by rising debt, with borrowings climbing to Rs 375 Cr in September 2026 from Rs 343 Cr a year earlier [E29], and a complete absence of shareholder returns via dividends at 0.00% [E3]. Operational consistency also shows cracks, as both yearly and quarterly operating-margin trends are flagged as inconsistent [E22, E23], alongside specific screening flags highlighting a 20% drop in sales YoY and a 26% drop in net profit YoY [E50, E49]. Furthermore, technical momentum is weak, with the stock sitting below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E40], and the rules-based screen scoring a mediocre 58 out of 100 with low confidence [E44]. Conceded: [E35].

Conceded: [E28], [E3], and [E40]. While the current ratio stands at 0.97x [E28] and borrowings rose to Rs 375 Cr [E29], the company generated robust operating cash flow of Rs 141 Cr with a high cash conversion of 1.76x, proving profits are fully backed by cash [E24, E25]. The rise in borrowings also supports future capacity expansion, evidenced by Capital Work in Progress standing at Rs 189 Cr [E30]. On operational performance, screen flags regarding short-term drops [E49, E50] are completely overshadowed by strong multi-year compounding, featuring a 3-year sales growth of 14% and 3-year profit growth of 26% [E13, E15]. Furthermore, technical moving averages [E40] and rules-based scores [E44] ignore the massive intrinsic value buffer, as a reverse DCF shows the current price absurdly prices in negative earnings growth of -0.9% [E37].

Conceded: [E24], [E25], and [E37]. Although cash conversion is reported at 1.76x with Rs 141 Cr in operating cash flow [E24, E25], free cash flow collapses to just Rs 8 Cr [E26], leaving virtually no unencumbered cash after capital requirements. Furthermore, pointing to the reverse DCF [E37] ignores glaring short-term contractions where net profit fell -26% YoY and sales dropped -20% YoY [E49, E50]. The bull's dismissal of balance sheet risks is also dangerous given that short-term obligations already exceed short-term assets with a current ratio of 0.97x [E28], while total borrowings continue to swell to Rs 375 Cr [E29]. Finally, while multi-year trends are cited [E13, E15], the actual operating-margin trend is explicitly flagged as inconsistent across both yearly and quarterly horizons [E22, E23], and the stock sits below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E40].
